notes: All metadata and content judgements come from sources retrieved in this session (URLs listed in verification_method). No candidates rejected; no duplicates within the batch. OpenAlex was unavailable (daily budget exceeded) and the arXiv export API returned empty results, so abstracts came from Crossref (IonBench, SED-ML) and the Semantic Scholar Graph API (the four IEEE/ACM papers), cross-checked against arXiv abstract pages and arXiv PDF full text where available. IonBench full text read on journals.plos.org. The GlueTest full text is closed-access and was not read; only its abstract and artifact repository metadata were used. Minor name variants versus the input (SED-ML: Crossref lists 'Richard Adams' and 'Frank T Bergmann') were resolved in favour of Crossref. For Dhruv & Dubey, the arXiv preprint is dated 2024-10-31 and the PASC proceedings version 2025 (Crossref); 2025 is used.

rows.citation: Owen MJ, Mirams GR (2025). IonBench: A benchmark of optimisation strategies for mathematical models of ion channel currents. PLOS Computational Biology 21(8):e1013319.
rows.model_type: cardiac ion-channel current ODE models (Hodgkin-Huxley and Markov formulations) under voltage clamp
rows.controlled_mutations: no - benchmarks parameter-fitting optimisers on five fixed problems; no deliberate single-fault model mutants or fault-detection study.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - the suite spans problems with different voltage protocols (e.g. staircase, literature protocols), but protocols define fitting problems, not a detection battery.
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial - some cost functions use derived summary-statistic curves (Moreno problem) instead of raw current traces; no spiking features, no eFEL.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - optimises model parameters and ranks 34 optimisation approaches by expected run time; protocols are fixed, not selected.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - compares approaches across all benchmark problems; no discovery/held-out split of models or fault families was found.
rows.ai_transformations: no - no AI-assisted model editing or code transformation.
rows.software: ionBench - https://github.com/CardiacModelling/ionBench (BSD-3-Clause per GitHub API; archived v1.0.1 at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.15754015)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Solves inverse parameter fitting for cardiac channel models; NeuroSem instead detects behavioural drift after edits to neuron models with current-clamp batteries. Relevant only as a reproducible-benchmark design reference.
rows.verification_method: Crossref https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1371/journal.pcbi.1013319 (metadata + abstract); full text https://journals.plos.org/ploscompbiol/article?id=10.1371/journal.pcbi.1013319 (methods, data availability); GitHub REST https://api.github.com/repos/CardiacModelling/ionBench (license); DataCite https://api.datacite.org/dois/10.5281/zenodo.15754015 (archive).
rows.found_via: WebSearch site:ieeexplore.ieee.org ion channel model voltage protocol design model discrimination optimisation (bioRxiv link); verified via Crossref

rows.citation: Waltemath D, Adams R, Bergmann FT, et al. (2011). Reproducible computational biology experiments with SED-ML - The Simulation Experiment Description Markup Language. BMC Systems Biology 5:198.
rows.model_type: general computational biology simulation models (format-agnostic; SBML/CellML examples); simulation-experiment description standard
rows.controlled_mutations: no - SED-ML can encode model modifications applied before simulation, but for experiment reuse, not fault seeding or mutant testing.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - can describe several simulations and model changes; Level 1 Version 1 covers time-course simulations only, with no stimulus battery concept.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - defines output and post-processing descriptions generically; no electrophysiological feature extraction.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - an exchange format for encoding experiments; no protocol selection.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - format specification paper with interoperability demonstration; no evaluation split.
rows.software: SED-ML specification and resources - https://sed-ml.org/ (site lists Level 1 Version 5 as current)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Infrastructure for describing simulation experiments reproducibly. NeuroSem could encode its protocols in SED-ML or LEMS, but adds mutation-calibrated drift detection, tolerance calibration and protocol selection.
rows.verification_method: Crossref https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1186/1752-0509-5-198 (metadata + structured abstract); project site https://sed-ml.org/ (current version statement).

rows.citation: Dhruv A, Dubey A (2025). Leveraging Large Language Models for Code Translation and Software Development in Scientific Computing. Proceedings of the Platform for Advanced Scientific Computing Conference (PASC), pp. 1-9.
rows.model_type: general scientific software (legacy Fortran particle-physics simulation code translated to C++)
rows.controlled_mutations: no - no seeded faults or mutants; LLM output is reviewed, compiled and tested by developers.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no - correctness is checked with the codebase's existing tests; no systematic input or perturbation battery found.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - not a neuroscience or electrophysiology setting.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - focuses on prompt engineering and a translation workflow, not test selection.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - experience report comparing LLMs on conversion tasks; no held-out evaluation design found.
rows.ai_transformations: yes - LLM-assisted Fortran-to-C++ translation, Fortran-C API generation and code inspection via the CodeScribe tool.
rows.software: CodeScribe - https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.13879406 (Zenodo record 'akashdhruv/CodeScribe: 2024.09', CC-BY-4.0 per DataCite); results repo https://github.com/akashdhruv/llm-conversion-performance
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Shows LLM translation of science code needs correctness checks but relies on manual review and existing tests. NeuroSem would offer a domain-specific, mutation-calibrated behavioural check for AI-edited neuron models.
rows.verification_method: Crossref https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1145/3732775.3733572 (metadata, no abstract); Semantic Scholar Graph API DOI:10.1145/3732775.3733572 (abstract, arXiv ID); arXiv https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.24119 (authors/date) and PDF full text (tool links); DataCite https://api.datacite.org/dois/10.5281/zenodo.13879406; GitHub REST users/akashdhruv/repos.

rows.citation: Abid MS, Pawagi M, Adhikari S, et al. (2024). GlueTest: Testing Code Translation via Language Interoperability. 2024 IEEE International Conference on Software Maintenance and Evolution (ICSME), pp. 612-617.
rows.model_type: general software libraries (Java to Python translation of Apache Commons CLI and CSV)
rows.controlled_mutations: no - the abstract describes no seeded faults or mutation analysis; full text (closed access) not read.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - reuses the original test suites plus tests from client projects (30 for CLI, 6 for CSV) to exercise translated code.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - generic software unit tests; no scientific output features.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - no test selection or minimisation described in the abstract.
rows.heldout_evaluation: unclear - client-project tests act as extra validation, but no formal held-out design is described in the abstract.
rows.ai_transformations: unclear - motivated by LLM-era code translation; the abstract does not say whether the evaluated translations were produced by an LLM.
rows.software: GlueTest artifact - https://github.com/seal-research/gluetest (no license detected by GitHub API); uses GraalVM for interoperability
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Validates behaviour preservation of translated code by running untranslated original tests. NeuroSem targets neuron model files, uses electrophysiological behaviour with calibrated tolerances, and measures and optimises the battery's sensitivity with mutants.
rows.verification_method: Crossref https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1109/icsme58944.2024.00061 (metadata, full author list, pages); Semantic Scholar Graph API DOI:10.1109/ICSME58944.2024.00061 (abstract); GitHub REST repos/seal-research/gluetest (artifact, license field null).
rows.found_via: WebSearch site:ieeexplore.ieee.org large language model translation scientific code simulation behavior preservation testing; verified via Crossref

rows.citation: Straubinger P, Kreis M, Lukasczyk S, et al. (2025). Mutation Testing via Iterative Large Language Model-Driven Scientific Debugging. 2025 IEEE International Conference on Software Testing, Verification and Validation Workshops (ICSTW), pp. 358-367.
rows.model_type: general software (modules from ten open-source Python projects)
rows.controlled_mutations: yes - Cosmic Ray generates mutants; up to 1,000 sampled per project; LLMs try to kill mutants or argue equivalence.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - generated tests supply varied program inputs per mutant; no physical stimulation protocols.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - assertions on generic program outputs; mutation score and code coverage as metrics.
rows.protocol_optimization: partial - iteratively refines individual tests until a mutant is killed; no budgeted selection of a compact test battery.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - compares four approaches on the same ten projects; no held-out model or mutation-family split found.
rows.ai_transformations: partial - LLMs generate and refine tests, not model or code transformations whose behaviour preservation is checked.
rows.software: Replication package - https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.28550855 (CC-BY-4.0 per DataCite); baselines use Pynguin https://github.com/se2p/pynguin and Cosmic Ray
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Uses mutants to assess and drive LLM test generation for generic Python code. NeuroSem applies mutant-based adequacy to neuron models, with electrophysiology features, numerical tolerances, greedy protocol selection and held-out generalisation.
rows.verification_method: Crossref https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1109/icstw64639.2025.10962485 (metadata, pages); Semantic Scholar Graph API DOI:10.1109/ICSTW64639.2025.10962485 (abstract); arXiv https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.08182 (authors/date) and PDF full text (subjects, Cosmic Ray, equivalent-mutant handling); DataCite https://api.datacite.org/dois/10.6084/m9.figshare.28550855.
rows.found_via: WebSearch site:ieeexplore.ieee.org mutation testing scientific software simulation models; verified via Crossref | Crossref 'mutation testing scientific software'; DataCite (arXiv); verified via Crossref + DataCite abstract

rows.citation: Ma L, Zhang F, Sun J, et al. (2018). DeepMutation: Mutation Testing of Deep Learning Systems. 2018 IEEE 29th International Symposium on Software Reliability Engineering (ISSRE), pp. 100-111.
rows.model_type: artificial deep neural networks (image classifiers on MNIST and CIFAR-10); not biophysical neuron models
rows.controlled_mutations: yes - source-level (training data/program) and model-level operators, e.g. Gaussian weight fuzzing, neuron effect block, neuron switch, layer deactivation.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - test datasets of many input images serve as stimuli; no electrical stimulation protocols.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - classification outputs and mutation scores; 'neuron' refers to artificial network units.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - measures test-data quality via mutant detection; no budgeted selection of test inputs described in the abstract.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - demonstrated on two datasets with three models; no held-out model or mutation-family generalisation design found.
rows.ai_transformations: no - the systems under test are ML models; no AI-assisted code or model transformations.
rows.software: none - no project code link found in the arXiv version (GitHub URLs there are cited references only)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Terminology collision: mutates artificial neural networks to grade test data. NeuroSem mutates biophysical NeuroML neuron models, compares electrophysiology features under calibrated tolerances, and selects stimulation protocols evaluated on held-out models.
rows.verification_method: Crossref https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1109/issre.2018.00021 (metadata, pages); Semantic Scholar Graph API DOI:10.1109/ISSRE.2018.00021 (abstract); arXiv https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.05206 (authors/date/comment) and PDF full text (operator table, link check).
rows.found_via: WebSearch site:ieeexplore.ieee.org NeuroML mutation testing; site:ieeexplore.ieee.org mutation testing computational neuroscience; verified via Crossref
